transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. This is not a DIY job for you to fix yourself. Because this involves gas components, any repair must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer. The most likely cause is that the safety device (flame failure device) isn't detecting the flame once you release the knob, so it shuts off the gas supply as a precaution. This can sometimes happen if the burner cap is slightly misaligned or dirty, preventing the flame from properly touching the sensor. Before calling an engineer, please check this simple thing: Look inside the oven at the burner (the metal piece where the flame comes out). Is there a small metal cap sitting over it? Ensure it is seated perfectly flat and dry. If it looks wet or crooked, try re-seating it gently. If you have checked that and the problem persists, please contact a Gas Safe engineer to replace the faulty safety component.

I've had a look and I can't see anything out of place with the burner. I did notice some burnt-on fat around the base of it near the little probe, though. I only smell gas briefly while I'm trying to light it, and my CO alarm in the kitchen hasn't gone off.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Flame failure device (thermocouple) not detecting flame (high)
Dirty or misaligned burner cap preventing proper ignition/flame sensing (medium)

The fault they reported is: "oven flame goes out when knob is released". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (gas work): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
